content.label: It actually did exactly what I was hoping, understanding the native limitations of the iPhone ecosystem.  Only one without subscription!

title.label: Solid app that does what it says perfectly

content.label:
Great app. Does what it says, straight forward and easy to set up.

I have one suggestion which is to allow more color options for the background. I understand it would make the dock background look visible but a workaround would be maybe adding text/art to the dock area as part of the wallpaper or adding some kind of styling that makes it look like it’s not a dock.

Even without the suggestion this is a 5 star app because it works exactly how it’s described and helps achieve the goal of minimizing distractions

So far, I enjoy this a lot. Seems like a good compromise between the Light Phone interface with the functionality of the iPhone. I don’t mind it jumping to shortcuts, but of course I would love if it didn’t (thanks apple).

Here is an improvement I would love to see that does not seem like it would be difficult to implement:

Various widget sizes. It would be nice to have the big square on top with the medium size rectangle on the bottom to have 2 widgets on one screen (iPhone 12 mini if that helps)

I do have one actual issue, the supplied background is slightly different than the dark mode widget and dock. It is just so slightly off that I can see the border of the widget and dock. I have made sure blur is off and no ‘reduce transparency mode is enabled’

title.label: Minimalist, simple and easy to use

content.label:
Once I got the app settup it made my iPhone use so much easier. It’s like reading a book.
I dont have to navigate the chaos that is my apps or app folder. 
I have 3 pages.
1 organized with the productivity tools I use in a daily basis. Another page I use for all my communication and messaging apps. And a third I use for the more recreational apps like camera or a metronome for music, as well as my gdrive.
It would be great if the app could create 2 or 3 more pages for additional organization and spacing.

Makes my tech addiction that much more easier to control.
Thanks!
Needed an app to clean up my Home Screen a bit and so far this fits the bill. Only used it for an hour so far so we’ll see how it goes.

title.label: The app is way too buggy for this price

content.label: After buying the app to test I have came to a conclusion it is a very good idea, but there are too many bugs on the app plus for its simplicity of an app I would feel as if the concept should have been complete before the launch of this application. The short cuts don’t work with full ui of apple , a lot of the shortcuts take you to random places in the application you want to go to.

I’m trying to get this set up. I’ve been working on it all morning. Some of the apps on iPhone need to go through shortcuts and it’s not opening on my phone like in the tutorial video. I’ve tried everything and I’m frustrated and there’s no contact info so that I can get help.
This is a great app to help reduce my phones addictive nature. It was very easy to setup and works as promised. The developer seems very active in rolling out updates which is always a plus.

title.label: My apps are not in the list

content.label: Thought this would be a list of my apps. Seems like a bug.

The widget is too small. It doesn't seem scaled properly. I see another review citing this issue with a response from the author back in April. Multiple shortcuts are needed because the text is too small when you have many apps listed.

I came across this app in a post about how to reduce phone usage.  It’s awesome, basically exactly like I would hope this type of app would work.  I’ve only had it for a day or so, but I think the main value is just changing the default experience you have when you open your phone.   By reducing your home screen to a plain list, you interact with your phone with a much more intentional way.  Thanks to the developer for making such an awesome app.
You’re paying for widgets and shortcuts. The rest is wallpaper and dark mode. Nothing special.

title.label: Needs a blank spacer and better fonts

content.label: If they added a spacer and better fonts it would be perfect.

First app I’ve actually taken the time to right a review. If you’re looking to Dumbify your phone this does exactly that. The premise here is you match the background with the widget color, which the app provides and then declutter your Home Screen. 

It takes a minute to get used to as you’re adjusting yourself to how you’ve always used your phone. You can still access all of your apps and the smart part of your device. This just adds points of friction so you aren’t on autopilot to do those mindless scrolls. 

How the app functions does mean there is a bit of lag every time you do something so that snappy feel that Apple has gotten you accustomed too will go away. I’ll keep testing but as for the first night I’m very pleased and not bothered. 

I’ve seen some comments that already offer some great ideas so I’m hoping overtime there is still some support to keep my phone from controlling my life, but also being useful.

title.label: Slow loading shortcuts widget, doesn’t truly block app shortcuts

content.label: This app is a simple widget. The shortcuts look ugly when they load which is contradictory to the aesthetic promised, and they take too long to load compared to just loading them as is. It’s a good idea in theory, not application. There are hardly any installed shortcuts to most mainstream mail and other apps, so you will be spending too much time creating custom shortcuts if you keep this, and you can make shortcuts on your own for free. There is no point to the app which doesn’t block out other apps. When your device slides to the right, it looks and acts like you never installed the widget. Fair, but I wasn’t expecting that this is just a widget app and not something to block out everything like a mock operating system. An app within an app, you know? I feel bad but this really isn’t worth it. The distractions are going to be there when you slide your finger to the right and the device shows you the apps you have installed anyway with the regular style of the original Home Screen style layout. Would not recommend. I feel so bad writing this review because the intentions seem honest. It’s better to go out and buy yourself a dumb device or, as mentioned, make shortcuts with a black or white background image for free. There is an expensive dumb smartphone out by some Swiss brand called Punk MC02 that does this but works quickly. It’s too pricy for me to spend for minimalism and alleged tech privacy when I can use a computer, but it will do the job better and is the formatting that this app developer uhhh….took lots of “inspiration” from, to phrase it politely. Look it up on the web and the typeface plus more will all be a bit familiar to this. But the difference is, it would probably work as promised. Seeing the app developer here insists to click reduce motion. Uh nope, this doesn’t make your shortcuts widget any faster… it just is SLOW, never anything decent.
Great app for money compared to competitors, the dev is very active and I’m looking forward to having multiple widgets!

You can get the other free app, I forget the name that is basically like this one for free and has better design. The design of this one is bad, you can only add so many apps before it cuts off and there's nothing you can do about it. This should be free, I'm requesting a refund.

I’ve been trying to dumbify my phone in fits and starts for a while now. I was in another fit and start a couple days ago. I tried one app I had read about but it was clunky to use and couldn’t find/link to simple apps that come with the iPhone. Found another and tried it and the process was convoluted and confusing. While trying to find out how to work it, I discovered Dumbify. It is heads and tails over anything else I’ve seen or tried. Simple, elegant user interface. In just two days, my phone use has already gone down. 

I asked a question on the Reddit post where I discovered the app, and the developer was quick to respond, which was awesome. 

A few (not all) of the iPhone native apps require going though Shortcuts (this is an Apple thing, not a Dumbify thing), and seeing that burst of color interrupt my calm minimalist phone drives me bonkers. It’s very quick and temporary, but come on, Apple!

I saw ads for a lot of similar apps on Instagram but they were all early access or subscription nonsense. Then I stumbled across this app and was quite delighted! There's not a whole lot to say; the app does exactly what it says, and does it well. It's gotten my screen time down, which is what I was hoping to see. Waiting for multi-page support, but I've stop-gapped that with a few Shortcuts for now. If you're looking to spend less time on your phone, give this a try!

This app is really great considering it’s still in an early version. 
The creator is really reactive on the feedback and I’m sure it will soon be better than Blank Spaces App for a fifth of the price !

title.label: Best App on the App Store

content.label:
This works so well that it blows my mind away. The workaround using Shortcuts is a little jank but worth it considering the decreased noise on the home screen.

A feature idea I have is for a weather widget in the same style. A text only weather widget would look great.

Thanks for this amazing app fr <3
Feel like I’m missing something, this app is slow to work, quickly apparent that this won’t work for me
Love the idea - I’ve already been enjoying the benefits of using Dumbify to minimize the everyday “noise” from the seemingly nonstop stream of notifications.

Overall works very well with one small gripe. 
I’d like the widget to either be full screen or half screen to allow placing two widgets on my iPhone SE. I added too many apps, and the names are now overflowing outside of the widget. Currently I can only place 10 apps and I wanted 11!

It also looks like the Settings app doesn’t launch to the main page.

This app feels a lot like Blankspaces, but with some nice improvements and a reasonable price. My only request would be to add the ability to have multiple pages of items. The small text items for larger lists can get annoying. Overall, great work!
Love it so far. Excited to see what’s else is in store!
It’s like On Point but better
